Duration::total().milliseconds()¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

DurationTotal Duration::total() const;
Series DurationTotal::milliseconds() const;

What It Does¶

Converts a Duration’s elapsed magnitude into a plain Series expressed in milliseconds — total().nanoseconds() divided by 1'000'000. See total().nanoseconds() for the full explanation of the total() accessor.

Parameters¶

None — this is a zero-argument accessor on self.

Returns¶

Series A floating-point Series at self’s shape, in milliseconds.

Examples¶

Example 1. A 90-minute Duration read as milliseconds.

auto ninety_min = pluss::duration::minutes(90);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(ninety_min.total().milliseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=5.4000e+06

90 minutes is 5.4 * 10^6 milliseconds.

Notes¶

  • .total().milliseconds() never rounds or truncates — the result is always the exact (floating-point) division.

See Also¶

  • total().microseconds(): the finer unit this divides.

  • total().seconds(): the next unit up.
